usageNotes: Use this to add a Ceph Monitor (and, for the very first monitor, also a Ceph Manager) to an existing Ceph cluster on a given PVE node. The target node must be online and already have Ceph installed; the caller requires Sys.Modify at the root level. Returns a task UPID string — poll the task API to confirm the monitor comes up before continuing with additional cluster changes.

examples.summary: Add a monitor on pve2 using the node name as the monitor ID

tips: Omitting monid defaults it to the node name, which is the standard Ceph convention and avoids ID mismatches.
Only supply mon-address if autodetection picks the wrong interface (e.g., on multi-homed nodes where the storage/Ceph network differs from the management network).
A healthy Ceph cluster requires an odd number of monitors (3 or 5) for quorum; plan additions accordingly.
The first monitor created on a fresh cluster also auto-creates a Manager (ceph-mgr) process on the same node.
